title: Developing Techniques for Focused Ion Beam Milling and In-Situ Micro-Compression to Characterize Orientation-Dependent Mechanical Properties of Molecular Crystals
content: This presentation focuses on the development of advanced micromechanical testing techniques aimed at characterizing the properties of molecular crystal materials (MCMs), which are held together by weak intermolecular forces such as hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces. MCMs are critical in various applications, including pharmaceuticals, explosives, and emerging optoelectronics. Despite their significance, the mechanical behavior of these materials, particularly regarding crystallographic orientation and mobile defects at the onset of plasticity and fracture, remains poorly understood. To address these challenges, we are innovating techniques that utilize focused ion beam (FIB) milling to fabricate micropillars from individual inorganic MCM crystals. This method allows for precise control over the microstructural features of the samples, enabling us to conduct in situ compression tests observed with a scanning electron microscope (SEM). By systematically varying the fabrication parameters and testing conditions, we aim to establish a robust methodology for linking mechanical properties to microstructural characteristics and crystallographic orientation. This research not only enhances our understanding of the mechanical behavior of MCMs but also contributes to the advancement of FIB and Micromechanical compression testing methodologies [1].
